title: Build vs Buy for a Core Enterprise Capability
decision: Prefer buy/configure when the capability is non-differentiating and mature products cover the operating model; build when integration, national-scale process specificity or strategic control creates material differentiation.
questions: Is the capability strategically differentiating?
Can the product fit governance and integration constraints?
What is the 3-year TCO including change, vendor lock-in and support?
Can we exit or replace it without operational disruption?
evidence: Enterprise architecture and vendor governance across national platforms.

title: Stabilizing a Delayed Technology Program
decision: Stabilize scope, ownership, dependencies and production risk before accelerating delivery. Speed without control compounds delay.
questions: What outcomes are truly critical?
Where is decision latency?
Which dependencies sit outside the team?
What can be delivered safely in 30 days?
evidence: Program governance, service readiness and cross-team delivery leadership.

title: Governing AI Adoption
decision: Treat AI as a governed business capability: define purpose, data boundaries, human accountability, evaluation, monitoring and exit criteria before scaling.
questions: What decision or task is being augmented?
What harm follows from an incorrect output?
Which data is allowed?
Who owns approval and monitoring?
evidence: Digital governance, data governance and public-sector technology leadership.

title: Modernizing Legacy Applications
decision: Modernize by business capability and risk—not by technology age alone. Use strangler patterns, integration boundaries and measurable service outcomes.
questions: Which capabilities create operational risk?
Where are coupling and data ownership problems?
What can be isolated first?
How will service continuity be protected?
evidence: Enterprise applications, integration architecture and production operations.

title: Consolidating Fragmented Data Platforms
decision: Start with ownership, semantics, data quality and consumption needs before selecting a target platform. Consolidation without governance recreates fragmentation centrally.
questions: Who owns each critical data domain?
Which definitions conflict?
What latency is required?
Which executive decisions depend on the data?
evidence: National health data warehouse and analytics architecture.
